Victor Boniface’s Bayer Leverkusen career appears to be approaching a breaking point, with the Nigerian striker reduced to just 15 minutes of action this season after falling to third choice in the club’s attacking pecking order, PUNCH Sports Extra reports. Leverkusen sporting director Simon Rolfes has admitted that a January departure is a possibility, with the club seemingly open to ending the striker’s increasingly frustrating spell at the BayArena. “His competition for places isn’t easy. A move in the winter is definitely an option. Boni is fully fit. He’s participated in everything since June,” Rolfes said. Despite Rolfes’ assurances about his fitness and a promising pre-season, Boniface has managed only 15 minutes across all competitions this campaign, featuring for seven minutes against Stuttgart, three against Nuremberg and five against Elversberg. Sky Sport Germany journalist Florian Plettenberg reported that the 25-year-old is keen to leave Leverkusen in January in search of regular playing time. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. The situation is now becoming more concrete,” Plettenberg wrote. “Boniface is under contract until 2028 and currently ranks as Leverkusen’s third-choice striker.” Boniface was one of Leverkusen’s standout performers during their historic double-winning 2023/24 campaign under Xabi Alonso, scoring 21 goals and providing nine assists in 34 appearances across all competitions. He managed 10 goals and two assists in 26 appearances during the 2024/25 season before being deemed surplus to requirements and sent on loan to Werder Bremen for the 2025/26 campaign. His spell in Bremen proved equally difficult, and he returned to Leverkusen ahead of the current season while recovering from knee surgery. Although he has since worked his way back to full fitness, opportunities in the first team have remained limited. Before his loan move to Bremen, several clubs in the Middle East had reportedly expressed interest in signing the Nigerian. In January 2025, a proposed move to Cristiano Ronaldo’s Al-Nassr fell through at the final hurdle, with a transfer fee of €70m reportedly under discussion. With no formal offers yet confirmed, it remains to be seen whether Boniface will secure another loan move or pursue a permanent departure in January. Leverkusen signed him from Belgian side Royale Union Saint-Gilloise for €20.5m in the summer of 2023, and his current contract runs until 2028.
